items.description: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development. About the Role As the founding Deployment Lead Manager for Asia Pacific outside Japan, you’ll lead and grow a team of DLs already working with customers across the region. Based in Singapore, you’ll partner with regional FDE and go-to-market leaders to decide which opportunities to pursue and where your team can have the greatest impact. On the most important engagements, you’ll work directly with DLs, engineers and customers to shape the scope, win the work and deliver it through production and adoption. You’ll help build the function as you lead it, navigating significant ambiguity and giving DLs the support and autonomy to lead in their own markets. You’ll partner with FDE, Product, Research, and GTM to balance customer-specific solutions with reusable capabilities and ensure field insights inform product priorities. Drawing on your experience leading complex technical deployments and products, you’ll guide decisions on scope, feasibility, sequencing, and delivery readiness, helping your team make sound tradeoffs and build lasting customer trust. Success will be measured by the impact of your team’s deployments, the growth of your DLs, and how effectively the team and delivery model scale. This role is based in Singapore. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. This role will require travel up to 25%. In this role, you will: - Lead and grow a team of DLs delivering production systems with frontier models - Own end-to-end delivery outcomes, from scoping through production, adoption, and handoff - Help DLs and FDEs shape and win strategic engagements, then deliver the outcomes they committed to with the customer. - Codify what works into practical playbooks, consistent delivery practices, and product roadmap inputs - Set a high bar for DL performance through hands-on coaching, actionable feedback, and career development - Make staffing decisions across markets with regional FDE leaders. Give local DLs clear ownership, step into critical pursuits and deployments where they need your help, and identify where the team needs to hire next. You might thrive in this role if you - Bring 8+ years of customer-facing technical delivery or product leadership experience, including 2+ years managing high-performing teams. - Have personally led complex technical deployments from prototype through production, adoption, and handoff. You’ve also helped win or expand an engagement by shaping the scope with engineers, influencing what the customer chose to fund, and delivering against the commitments you helped make. - Have a strong product mindset, ideally with product management experience, and can balance customer-specific needs with reusable solutions. - You’ve built or grown a customer-facing technical team across multiple markets. You can point to an engagement you helped land and deliver yourself, and one where someone you developed took the lead. - Build deep trust across technical teams, Product, Research, GTM, and customer leadership. - Have a strong track record of hiring, coaching, and developing technical, customer-facing talent; elevate team performance through clarity, not process. items.title: Social Media Manager, Dicey
items.description: Who we are Magic Eden became one of the fastest companies in history to reach unicorn status, just 9 months after launch. Now we've taken that energy into our next chapter: Dicey, our crypto casino and sportsbook disrupting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets. We build our own tech in-house, and we use blockchain as a payment rail for faster, more secure, more transparent transactions. The role Most iGaming brands sound exactly the same. We're hiring someone to make sure Dicey never does. You'll be the voice of Dicey on social every day, X first. You come up with the ideas, make most of the content yourself, and own the voice, output and growth of our main accounts. You'll report to our Marketing Lead, who sets the strategy, and you'll get full autonomy on how we show up. Think of the coolest person at the party. Everyone wants to talk to them, they always have the line, and they never lose their composure when things get messy. That's the account we want. Basically, an organised degen. What you'll actually do - Run Dicey's main accounts day to day, with X as the priority: posting, replying, trend-jacking and community. - Come up with ideas. Lots of them. Turn launches, wins and world events into moments people share. - Make most of the content yourself: posts, memes, graphics and short-form video. Our creative team backs you up on bigger video production. - React in real time. When the internet moves, we're in it while it's still relevant. - Walk the line: edgy enough to be remembered, never at the expense of the brand. Know when to bite and when to let the FUD die on its own. - Build and run KOL partnerships that amplify what we're pushing through our main accounts. - Work with product on launches and announcements. - Track what's working and turn results into clear, simple reporting. You'll fit if - You're online too much and you know it. You live in internet culture, and you know iGaming Twitter and crypto Twitter are different crowds. - You write posts that are genuinely funny, sharp and on-trend, and you write them fast. - You make your own content. You don't need a designer or an editor to ship a meme, a graphic or a short video. - You know the difference between edgy and cringe, and between bold and brand-damaging. - Drama doesn't scare you. When Dicey gets pulled in, you handle it with precision and make sure we come out on top. - You've worked with KOLs or creators and know how to run a partnership that actually moves numbers. - You're comfortable with the numbers: reach, engagement, traffic, and what to do about them. - You're proactive. You don't need permission to have an idea, and you don't need chasing to deliver it. - You're comfortable working in online casino and sports betting. Nice to have - You're iGaming native. - You can show us posts or campaigns of yours that took off. - You can name the last brand that made you laugh on X. What you get - Full ownership of the voice of a brand that's growing fast. - Room to grow as the team grows. - Competitive compensation. - Remote, global team. The small print - If it goes viral, it was your idea. - If it flops, it was also your idea. Post the next one anyway.

items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Senior SAM Analyst on the CX Compliance team within Customer Experience, you’ll investigate complex financial crime activity and help strengthen AI-assisted investigations. You’ll own high-risk casework and apply human judgment to validate investigative outputs, support accurate regulatory reporting, and identify control gaps. Your findings will help Product, Compliance Technology, and ML Engineering improve investigation quality and efficiency while maintaining human oversight. What you’ll do: Own end-to-end anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CTF) investigations involving complex alerts, referrals, fraud typologies, and interconnected customer activity, including open-source research, identity verification, prior filing reviews, and blockchain analysis where needed. Draft and review investigative narratives and Suspicious Activity Reports/Transactions Reports (SARs/STRs), ensuring conclusions are evidence-based, clearly documented, and consistent with applicable requirements. Evaluate AI-generated narratives, evidence, risk assessments, and recommended dispositions using human-in-the-loop (HITL) quality scorecards to capture missed risk indicators, unsupported or fabricated facts, incorrect risk weighting, and inappropriate escalation decisions. Translate recurring investigation, model, data, and workflow defects into actionable feedback for Product, Compliance Technology, and ML Engineering. Support AI evaluation and release testing through annotation, calibration, user acceptance testing, and curated benchmark case reviews that inform model tuning and launch-readiness assessments. Escalate material issues affecting customers, regulatory filings, control effectiveness, or launch readiness, documenting evidence, potential impact, and recommended next steps. Required Skills and Experience: 4+ years of experience in AML, transaction monitoring, fraud investigations, or financial crime compliance, including independent ownership of complex, high-risk, or multi-entity cases. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated experience drafting and reviewing SARs/STRs and defending investigative conclusions through documented evidence and applicable regulatory requirements. Experience conducting quality reviews, second-reviewer checks, calibration, user acceptance testing, or model evaluation, including identifying systemic weaknesses and communicating reproducible, actionable findings. Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing cases and make risk-based escalation decisions under ambiguity or time pressure. Preferred: CAMS or another relevant AML, fraud, or crypto investigation certification; experience with SQL, Snowflake, fraud-ring analysis, entity resolution, or blockchain analytics. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.title: Managing Editor
items.location_text: United States, Seattle, New York, California, Toronto
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role summary: The Managing Editor runs the operational engine of the editorial team. This role turns strategy and drafts into a functioning production pipeline across all content streams (thought leadership, developer content, customer stories, product marketing content, etc.). This person is most responsible for whether things ship on time and at a consistent bar. Core responsibilities: - In conjunction with Editorial Content Director, own and maintain the master editorial calendar across all content streams, sequencing work so there is no competition for the same limited writing capacity - Manage the brief-to-publish workflow: assigning work, setting deadlines, tracking status, unblocking bottlenecks - Own the review/approval routing for each content type: legal and PR for thought leadership, engineering/DevRel sign-off for developer content, customer and legal approval for customer stories, product marketing alignment for product content - Set and enforce production-level style and quality standards (distinct from the Content Strategist's audience/strategy standards) - Manage relationships with freelancers, contractors, and cross-functional SME contributors who feed content into the pipeline - items.title: UX Researcher
items.description: Kick-start your career in the online gaming world and experience the very latest in technology and innovation. Who we are We’re Super Group, the NYSE-listed digital gaming company behind some of the world’s leading Sports and iGaming brands, including Betway and Jackpot City. We’re a powerhouse built on decades of expertise and we’re changing the game for good. Our mission is to give our customers a superclass entertainment experience. Who we’re looking for We’re on a thrilling journey of growth and innovation, and we need passionate, driven individuals to join us. At Super Group International, every day is action-packed, and we expect you to bring your A-game. In return, you’ll find a supportive environment where your skills can flourish and your career can soar. Ready to become a game-changer? Supercharge your career with us and be part of something extraordinary. Why we need you We’re building experiences that wow our customers – and that starts with bold, curious people who want to do work that matters. If you’re hungry to grow, excited by impact and ready for a challenge that will supercharge your career, this could be your moment. This is a mid-level role. User Researchers are dedicated to understanding the needs, behaviours and preferences of customers to inform the design and development of our products across all our remits: sports betting, casino and the platform they share. Your primary focus will be on generating actionable insights from your research to improve the user experience and drive the business forward. User Researchers play a crucial role in ensuring that the design and development align with user needs and expectations. Your work will inform decisions, reduce design guesswork, and ultimately lead to better products for our customers. What you’ll do You’ll take ownership of work that gives us our competitive edge, including: Project and Strategic Research: Run research on specific projects and features, and contribute research that helps shape the longer-term vision for design, product and the business, from opportunity areas to roadmap priorities. Customer-Centric Metrics: Establish and maintain metrics such as Net Promoter Score (NPS) and Customer Effort Score (CES) to measure customer satisfaction and loyalty. User Interviews: Conduct one-on-one interviews with users to gain in-depth insights into their goals, pain points, and expectations. Surveys and Questionnaires: Create surveys and questionnaires to gather quantitative data and feedback from a larger user base. Persona Development: Develop user personas based on research findings to guide design and development strategies. Observation and Usability Testing: Observe users in both controlled environments and real-world scenarios, conducting usability tests to uncover issues and opportunities for improvement. Product & Feature Research: Conduct research on current features and products across our remits to understand what creates the most value for our players. Insight Generation: Analyze and synthesize research data to produce meaningful insights, informing product roadmaps and strategy. Research Operations: Recruit and manage participants, handle consent, recordings and data in line with our privacy obligations, and keep findings findable in a shared research repository. Supporting the Team: Help designers and product managers plan and run their own studies, so research scales across the team. Collaboration with Teams: Work closely with designers, product managers, and developers to integrate user research into the product development process from concept to launch. Feedback Loops: Establish continuous feedback loops through player interviews, customer support collaboration, and in-product surveys to maintain up-to-date insights. Competitive Analysis: Research competitors’ products to identify trends and areas for differentiation, helping the business stay competitive in the market. Presenting Insights: Regularly present research findings and actionable recommendations to cross-functional teams. This list covers your core responsibilities – with plenty of room to stretch, explore and take on new challenges as we grow. What you’ll bring You’re someone who brings: · Clear, confident communication (written and verbal), and the ability to breakdown complex ideas · A collaborative mindset, working smoothly with cross‑functional teams to hit shared goals · Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects without dropping the ball · Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to high‑quality work · Adaptability – you stay sharp, productive and positive in fast‑moving environments Experience in UX Research: Proven experience conducting user research, interviews, usability testing, and analyzing both qualitative and quantitative data, especially in an iGaming context. Research Tools Proficiency: Proficient in UserTesting, Fullstory, Tableau and Figma. Desirable skills you’ve got up your sleeve It would be great if you also have some of the following skills: Knowledge of sports betting or casino products, including bet types, game mechanics and market trends Previous experience in the online gaming or casino industry, with a strong understanding of player behaviour and industry regulations Some familiarity with gambling regulations and compliance requirements Experience in developing and executing customer retention strategies Familiarity with behavioural analytics tools such as Fullstory Experience using AI tools such as Cursor, Make or Vercel v0 Experience with AI-assisted research, for analysis, synthesis or study setup Experience in the iGaming industry Formal education in Human-Computer Interaction or Psychology, or self-taught with a proven track record Our values are non-negotiables Our culture is underpinned by core values that are linked to key behavioural competencies. Along with the below behavioural competencies, these are essential for all employees in order for you to embed in and drive our culture forward. These competencies are: Adaptability Ownership and accountability Initiating action Resilience Team orientation Integrity Innovation What you’ll get back We invest in your growth and wellbeing, so you can bring your best: Supergrowth is real here. Our learning and development programmes give you the tools, training and opportunities to level up fast. Your progress matters . Our Performance tool ensures you get meaningful feedback to support your development and superdrive your career. Support that has your back . Our Employee Assistance Programme offers resources for you and your family. Private Health Care Life Insurance Ready to feel superclass? At Super Group, your experience matters. We’re honest, fair, and focused on helping you succeed – and your work will have real impact from day one. Game on! *Please note we will apply relevance to our Talent Management and Talent Development Programme as part of our recruitment process. *Shortlisted candidates may need to complete an assessment. This position requires trust and honesty it has access to customers financial details - therefore a credit and criminal record check will be conducted. The qualifications identified herein are an inherent job requirement; therefore, a qualification verification check will be done. By applying for this role, and supplying the necessary details, you hereby grant us permission to apply for these checks. This will be done in a confidential manner, and solely for the purposes of verification. Should you not hear from us within 2 weeks, please deem your application as unsuccessful. The perfect place to work, play and grow!

items.title: Applied AI Architect, Cyber
items.description: About the Team The Applied AI Architecture team is responsible for helping developers and enterprises safely and effectively deploy OpenAI technologies in production. We act as trusted technical advisors and thought partners for customers, working side by side with their teams to identify high-value use cases, design practical architectures, and move from prototype to durable deployment. Cybersecurity is one of the most urgent domains where AI can help. Security teams are under pressure to reason across code, logs, infrastructure, tickets, alerts, and vulnerability data faster than ever. As frontier models become more capable, organizations need deep technical guidance on how to evaluate, validate, and safely deploy AI systems in security-critical workflows. About the Role We are looking for a Cybersecurity Applied AI Architect to partner with customers and help them apply OpenAI models, APIs, Codex, and agentic workflows to real cybersecurity use cases. You will work with CISOs, security executives, application security leaders, SOC teams, security engineering teams, and hands-on practitioners to identify where AI can create measurable security outcomes. This is a customer-facing technical role for someone who can move fluidly between executive strategy, practitioner-level cyber depth, and hands-on solution design. You will help customers evaluate and deploy workflows such as secure code review, vulnerability triage, threat modeling, remediation, SOC and incident response workflows, detection engineering, cloud security, GRC automation, and security validation. You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Research, and Security to turn customer needs into safe deployment patterns, reusable field assets, and product feedback. In this role, you will: - Deeply embed with strategic customers as the technical lead for AI-enabled cybersecurity workflows, serving as a trusted partner to both security executives and technical practitioners. - Lead discovery across AppSec, DevSecOps, vulnerability management, SOC/IR, detection engineering, red team, cloud security, identity, and GRC automation use cases. - Build and deliver customer-facing demos, prototypes, workshops, proofs of concept, and reference architectures using OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, and common security tools. - Scope pilots with clear success criteria, data requirements, workflow integrations, evaluation methods, security constraints, safety boundaries, and human approval points. - Advise customers on safe implementation patterns, including tool and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval, sandboxing, data handling, guardrails, telemetry, auditability, and approval-gated side effects. - Translate between CISO-level outcomes and practitioner-level implementation details so each audience understands value, risk, and practical next steps. - Create reusable field assets such as demo narratives, playbooks, FAQs, objection handling, qualification guides, assessment templates, and competitive positioning. - Validate, synthesize, and deliver high-signal feedback to Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and GTM teams based on recurring customer requirements, blockers, product gaps, and emerging cyber workflows. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 5+ years of technical consulting, solutions engineering, security architecture, cyber advisory, deployment engineering, professional services, or equivalent customer-facing technical experience. - Bring strong cybersecurity domain expertise across one or more areas such as application security, cloud security, identity, vulnerability management, secure SDLC, incident response, detection engineering, threat intelligence, red teaming, or security architecture. - Can communicate credibly with CISOs, CTOs, security executives, engineering leaders, and highly technical security practitioners. - Have hands-on experience building prototypes or production systems with APIs, Python or JavaScript, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, or other common security tooling. - Understand how to design AI workflows with retrieval, structured outputs, tool use, evals, guardrails, telemetry, sandboxing, and human-in-the-loop review. - Are comfortable scoping pilots from ambiguous customer pain, including success metrics, required data, workflow integrations, evaluation criteria, deployment assumptions, and decision gates. - Have evidence-first security judgment: you validate findings, separate true positives from noise, document assumptions, and avoid overstating model or security claims. - Own problems end-to-end, operate with high throughput across multiple concurrent customer projects, and know when to stay hands-on versus create reusable leverage for the broader field. - Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help colleagues, and a desire to do whatever it takes to make the team and our customers successful. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy https://cdn.openai.com/policies/global-employee-and-contractor-privacy-policy.pdf At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. items.location_text: New York City, NY | Seattle, WA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About Anthropic Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Agent Security's mission is to safely increase how much of the world's work agents can do, starting inside Anthropic. Claude now writes and ships code, runs experiments and acts on people's behalf, for hours at a time. How much more it can take on depends on how safely it can operate. If, in the worst case, an agent misbehaves, Anthropic and the public may bear the consequences. Our mandate is to mitigate this risk, and Anthropic’s mission depends on it. The Partnerships team pairs security engineers with the teams at Anthropic that build Claude, build agents and rely on agents. Those teams are our partners. When a team wants its agents to do more, we threat model the plan with them and build the controls together. Most of this has no playbook, so we have often created new controls from first principles. The ones that work become part of our toolbox, spread to other teams, and in some cases ship in our products. We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead this team of security engineers. This is first and foremost a people leadership role. Few have secured agents at scale, especially at a frontier lab, so we don't expect you to have done it. We do expect you to have led security engineering teams, and we care most about how you lead people and reason about security. This role operates at the frontier. Each model generation, and each new harness, brings new challenges. The number of teams building on agents keeps growing, and partner teams won't always agree with your calls. In return, you will have the chance to directly contribute to making transformative AI go well, which is the heart of our mission. Key responsibilities Hire, mentor and grow senior and staff security engineers, and raise the bar as the team scales Set the team's investment strategy, deciding which teams get embedded engineers, and for how long, as demand outgrows the team Support the team through high-stakes safety and security calls made under uncertainty and on tight timelines Balance long-term investment in shared controls against partner teams’ immediate asks Deliver large security migrations across all of Anthropic Work through difficult tradeoffs with partner teams in ways that build trust and understanding Representative Projects In the past, the team has: Invented a new kind of classifier-based control for agents partnering with an internal team to develop and roll it out Co-built a sandbox with a product team, choosing what to enforce first so that adoption stuck Defined the security standards for running agents across the company and partnered with many different teams on how to hit these standards Minimum qualifications Excellent people management skills. You've hired, developed and managed senior and staff engineers, grown engineers into staff or lead roles, and kept a team delivering through changing priorities. Deep security management experience. You've managed security engineering teams and answered to executives for risk and tradeoffs. Strong written and oral communication skills. You've explained hard tradeoffs to executives and to engineers in plain words. Resilience, emotional awareness, low ego and high empathy Experience leading large migrations and highly cross-functional work A willingness to dive into the details to tie-break complex trade-offs without any clear answer, and the ability to stand by these decisions Preferred qualifications Experience embedding security engineers with product, infrastructure or research teams, or running a security partnerships team Agent security or AI/ML security experience Familiarity with AI safety concepts and research Leading in hypergrowth The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Senior Product Manager on the Simple Trading team within the Consumer & Business group, you'll own core parts of the retail trading experience used by millions of customers every day. This team builds delightful user experiences and UIs that optimize the primary buy, sell, and convert flows that drive Coinbase's consumer trading business. You'll define the product vision for your area, ship high-impact improvements across web and mobile, and partner closely with Engineering, Design, and Data Science to make crypto and perpetuals/derivatives trading engaging, delightful, and more trustworthy for every user. What you'll do: Own the end-to-end product roadmap for your area of the Simple Trading experience, from discovery and definition of engaging user experiences through execution, launch, and iteration across web and mobile UIs and platforms. Drive measurable improvements in trading conversion, user engagement, and revenue by identifying friction points, running experiments, and shipping data-informed solutions at scale. Partner with Engineering, Design, and Data Science to deliver high-quality consumer trading experiences, balancing speed, reliability, and usability across core trading workflows. Shape the long-term product strategy for retail trading by synthesizing user research, market trends, regulatory requirements, and competitive dynamics into a clear, prioritized vision. Lead cross-functional alignment across Consumer Trade and partner teams, ensuring stakeholders across Tax, Legal, Compliance, and Finance are informed and engaged on key decisions. Required Skills and Experience: 5+ years of Product Management experience shipping UI-heavy consumer products at scale, including at least 2 years working on trading, fintech, or marketplace products where conversion and revenue metrics were primary success measures. Deep familiarity with retail trading products, order types, and user workflows, with the ability to articulate what makes a trading experience intuitive and trustworthy. Proven ability to define and execute a product roadmap in high-ambiguity environments, with demonstrated results in improving core user flows visited by millions of users. Deep expertise in experimentation methodology, including designing A/B tests, defining success metrics, and interpreting results to inform product decisions with minimal analyst support. Fluency with data tools (SQL, Amplitude, or similar) sufficient to self-serve analyses, build dashboards, and monitor product health independently. Track record of driving alignment across senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, translating complex trade-offs into clear recommendations that accelerate decision-making. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.title: GTM Enablement - Product
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. About the role We’re hiring our first Product Enablement specialist. You will join the Product & Technical Enablement team and help our go-to-market teams get ready for every product launch, across Agents, APIs, and Creative. You will support our global go-to-market teams. Your mission: help sellers understand, demo, and sell each new launch with confidence, with preparation that starts well before launch day. What sets this role apart: we’re looking for someone who knows our products well enough to demo them and sell them. You have used agents, APIs, or creative tools hands-on, and you can explain how they work and why they matter to customers. You blend that with sales, solutions engineering, or product marketing experience, so you can teach sellers how to use a product, how to demo it, and how to pitch it. This role sits within GTM Enablement and reports to the Product & Technical Enablement Lead. You will work in close partnership with: - Product marketing and engineering teams (keeping content accurate as the platform ships) - GTM enablement (aligning on shared onboarding infrastructure) You will support product enablement for our go-to-market teams across Agents, APIs, and Creative, with the most day-to-day focus on API and Creative launches. This is a full-stack role on a lean team: you’ll build content, deliver training, design practice environments, and flex across products as needed. What you’ll do - Support new product launches: get an early heads-up from product marketing, research, and engineering, follow releases from alpha through GA, and have training ready before launch day, not the week of - Build launch workshops: go beyond what shipped and why it matters, with hands-on workshops on how to use the product, how to demo it, and how to pitch the value - Support competitive enablement: turn product marketing battlecards into trainings, simulations, and demo workshops, so sellers can answer parity, differentiation, and value questions with confidence - Support product certification: help define what “product certified” means for GTM teams, and build the playbooks and training content that raise product confidence across the whole field, not only new hires - Support everboarding and onboarding: keep training tied to new releases and capabilities, and keep content current as products ship - Craft realistic practice environments: demo certifications, role-play scenarios, and customer simulations with scored feedback, built on our own agent technology - Operate AI-natively: use ElevenLabs’ own voice and agent technology to build training and practice environments; default to AI tools to build faster, and teach others to do the same - Measure what matters: define and track the percent of sellers certified within 2 weeks of GA, demo and pitch quality scores, and win rate and stage progression against named competitors, and use the data to improve each launch Requirements We’re looking for someone who knows our products well and can teach sellers to demo and sell them. You’ll thrive here if you: - Have 4-7+ years as an enterprise seller or solutions engineer, or as a seller who moved into product marketing or enablement, at a SaaS, platform, or API-first company - Are hands-on with agents, APIs, or creative tools, and understand at a conceptual level how they work - Have demoed and pitched technical products to customers, and can explain the value, not only the features - Have a track record of teaching, mentoring, or building training, in addition to your customer-facing work - Are comfortable building a program from scratch, with no playbook to inherit - Have credibility with sellers, built from time in the seat or supporting sellers directly, and work well with product marketing, research, and engineering teams - Communicate clearly and can adapt product material for different audiences without diluting it Bonus - Experience at a high-growth AI/ML, developer tools, or API-first company - Background in voice AI, conversational AI, or contact center technology - Vertical depth in financial services, healthcare, telecom or CCaaS, or at other AI companies - Hands-on experience with competing voice and agent platforms - Experience running workshops or labs for sellers or customers - Experience building role-play, simulation, or demo practice environments Location Remote-first, globally distributed role. Expect occasional travel to team hubs and onboarding sessions. Candidates should be able to work effectively across US and European time zones. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

LOCATION This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in North America, with the ability to operate in Americas timezones required. items.title: Incident Commander, Detection & Response - US
items.description: About the Team Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture. About the Role As an Incident Commander on Detection & Response, you’ll lead the response to complex security incidents affecting OpenAI’s intellectual property, customer data, and infrastructure. You’ll establish response priorities, coordinate technical work streams, drive containment and recovery decisions within agreed authority, and keep stakeholders informed as facts evolve. You’ll work with security and infrastructure teams across endpoints, identity, cloud, and compute environments, maintaining clear ownership and effective handoffs across time zones. Detection engineering knowledge is a supporting requirement: you’ll use telemetry and detection logic to assess evidence, identify visibility gaps, and guide improvements that make incident response more effective. In this role, you will: - Run incident command from initial assessment through containment, recovery, and closure, establishing severity, scope, response objectives, and escalation needs. - Assign work stream owners and coordinate investigation, containment, and recovery in parallel. Maintain a decision log and distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions. - Drive timely containment and recovery decisions with the appropriate owners, weighing security risk, evidence preservation, and operational impact within agreed decision rights. - Communicate incident status, impact, uncertainty, actions underway, and the next update to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. - Manage cross-time-zone handoffs with explicit command ownership, current status, outstanding risks, pending decisions, and next actions. - Improve response readiness through exercises, playbooks, and post-incident reviews; track agreed corrective actions with their owners. - Partner with detection engineers to evaluate telemetry and detection quality, close incident-related visibility gaps, and prioritize practical response automation. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have personally led complex security incidents as incident commander or an equivalent response lead, with clear examples of decisions, delegation, escalation, and outcomes. - Make sound decisions with incomplete information and revise them as evidence changes, balancing containment urgency with operational impact. - Coordinate responders across teams and time zones, resolve conflicting priorities, and maintain clear ownership during handoffs. - Communicate calmly and precisely under pressure, including concise stakeholder updates and explicit statements of uncertainty. - Have the security and infrastructure fundamentals to challenge investigation findings and assess containment and recovery options. - Understand detection engineering, including telemetry coverage, detection logic, false positives and false negatives, and validation. Can query and interpret evidence to support response decisions. - Turn incident lessons into practical improvements to readiness, playbooks, detection coverage, and response tooling. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role As a Fraud and Disputes Vendor Management Specialist, you will be responsible for the day-to-day management and performance of our external operations partners. You’ll serve as a key connection point between internal Operations teams and our vendors, ensuring expectations are clear, performance is understood, and issues are quickly identified and resolved. You’ll use data to monitor SLAs, productivity, quality, staffing, and other key performance indicators while partnering with vendors to develop and execute improvement plans. You’ll also support capacity planning, new program launches, training, and changes to existing operations as our business continues to scale. Available shift Monday through Friday; 8:00am – 5:00pm CT This role is based in our Chicago, IL, Denver, CO, Lake Mary, FL and Westlake, TX offices with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Manage day-to-day relationships with external operations partners and serve as a primary point of contact for operational needs. Monitor vendor performance across key metrics including SLA, productivity, quality, customer experience, attendance, and staffing. Lead recurring vendor performance reviews and ensure risks, trends, and opportunities have clear owners and action plans. Partner with Operations leaders and vendors on capacity planning, staffing forecasts, schedules, hiring, and training needs. Identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and partner with vendors to develop and track corrective action plans. Ensure vendors are prepared for new products, processes, policies, tooling changes, and volume growth. Partner with internal teams to communicate business priorities and translate them into clear expectations for vendor teams. Use operational data to identify trends, proactively flag risks, and recommend opportunities to improve performance and efficiency. Support vendor expansions, new lines of business, site launches, and other operational changes. Maintain strong governance and documentation around vendor performance, commitments, escalations, and operational changes. Partner with the Fraud and Disputes Teams, Operations Enablement, Risk, Compliance, Quality, Training, and other teams to ensure vendor operations meet internal standards and requirements. What you bring 2+ years of experience in vendor management, BPO operations, workforce management, operations, or a related role. Experience managing or partnering with outsourced operations teams is preferred. Strong analytical skills and experience using operational metrics to identify trends and drive performance improvements. items.title: Security Engineer, RF and Technical Surveillance Countermeasures
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Part of that footprint is the radio spectrum around and inside each site: what transmits there, what listens there, and what the equipment itself gives off. You'll be the engineer who owns that domain end to end: on-site RF monitoring and detection, technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) and emanations security, from the threat basis through the systems that make the spectrum observable, to sign-off before a site opens. The engineering is in the monitoring and in the tooling that proves the controls hold: the sensors, receivers and their placement, the site baselines, and the detection logic that turns a rogue transmitter or an unexpected emitter into an alert an analyst trusts. External specialist partners do the hands-on sweep and measurement work; you write the scope, direct them on site and decide whether their report stands. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, sensor health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations, construction and legal teams, and directly with site operators and landlords. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities On-site RF monitoring and detection: design and develop the monitoring at each site: sensor, receiver and antenna selection and placement, the spectrum monitoring architecture, site RF baselines and what keeps them current, and detections that reach the team's security monitoring platform as alerts analysts keep trusting Tools, automation and AI agents: build the detection and classification tooling, the instruments and software for checks between sweeps, the findings and evidence records behind them, and the agents that triage alerts and watch sensor health. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it Technical surveillance countermeasures: own TSCM end to end: sweep cadence by space sensitivity, event-driven triggers such as fit-out, room turnover or an incident, scope and acceptance criteria per sweep, and findings handled with evidence and closure an assessor accepts Emanations security: set the posture for sites: the assessment method, zoning and separation, and shielding, filtering and protected cabling where warranted, written into the team's design and build standards so a site can build to them and an assessor can verify them Wireless and device policy by zone: detect which radios are actually present where (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IoT, trunked radio) and produce the evidence that the policy holds on the floor Specialist partners: write the scope and the deliverable standard for sweep and assessment work, direct it on site, and decide in the acceptance review whether a report stands New sites and leases: carry RF and emanations requirements into design reviews, lease terms and pre-opening reviews, and sign off RF and emanations, including the pre-opening sweep and assessment, before a site opens Minimum qualifications Have built at least one RF monitoring or detection system end to end, from receiver and antenna choice through the software that turns captures into alerts Understand RF at the engineering level: propagation, modulation, spectrum analysis and antenna behavior, with hands-on use of the instruments that measure them, such as spectrum analyzers and software-defined radios Have planned and conducted TSCM sweeps yourself and can explain, from having done the work, what a sweep can and cannot find and how an adversary would get past it Have done RF security, TSCM or emanations work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet Read and review code, design the data systems behind detection and monitoring tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review Understand compromising emanations and what zoning, shielding and filtering each buy and cost, and write requirements for them that a construction team or a landlord can build to and an assessor can test Direct a specialist vendor without deferring to them: write the scope, check the work, reject a weak report Preferred qualifications Experience assessing compromising emanations and shielding or filtering tradeoffs in a live facility, and applying a formal emanations or counter-surveillance standard, government or commercial (TEMPEST, ICD 705 style construction requirements, or a corporate equivalent) Have built signal classification or spectrum analysis pipelines at scale, or tuned RF detections for a security operations workflow so operators kept trusting them Familiarity with airspace or drone RF detection, and with where it stops and on-site monitoring starts Experience at sites you did not fully control: colocation or multi-tenant facilities, where the RF environment and the walls are not yours alone Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual security work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Project Manager, Compute Transformation
items.description: About the Team The Transformation team at OpenAI partners with Finance, Infrastructure, Data, and Engineering to design and scale the business processes and systems that support our growth. Our work combines process design, systems thinking, and operational change to turn fragmented workflows into reliable, repeatable, and well-controlled operations. We work as embedded partners to Finance, Accounting, and Operations, shaping priorities and delivering improvements across core business processes. For compute, our focus is an accurate, connected view of contractual obligations, delivered capacity, usage, and cost that supports sound decisions and repeatable financial operations. About the Role As Program Manager, Compute Transformation, you will lead cross-functional initiatives that connect purchasing, operations, billing, accounting, and financial planning across our compute commitments and our data center initiatives. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of problem definition, process design, integrated planning, and end-to-end delivery. You will work across Compute Finance, Infrastructure Accounting, Capacity Planning, Fleet, Design & Construction, Operations, Procurement, Legal, Data, and Engineering. You will turn ambiguous business problems into clear requirements, drive decisions and dependencies, and deliver reliable processes and systems that make compute and infra spend easier to understand, forecast, reconcile, and control. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, with a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office. In this role, you will: - Own an integrated compute and infra transformation plan: workstreams, milestones, critical dependencies, resources, decision logs, and acceptance criteria. Drive execution from problem definition through production adoption. - Map current workflows and design scalable processes from demand planning, contracting, delivery & acceptance, receiving & operations, invoicing, payment, and month-end close. Clarify ownership, handoffs, evidence, and exception paths. - Enable source of truth systems that cover both operational needs and accounting / finance needs for data center construction, operations, and maintenance. - Drive consistent tracking of contracts, tranches, delivery events, and capacity acceptance. Connect committed spend to provisioned, accepted, allocated, and used capacity to support forecasting and financial review. - Coordinate reliable ingestion and normalization of cloud service provider usage, billing, invoice, and delivery data. Establish data owners, completeness checks, and traceability to financial outputs. - Improve compute billing, accrual, and allocation processes through consistent pricing rules, SKU mappings, telemetry and organizational tags, reconciliations, and controlled handling of manual adjustments. - Partner with application, AI, and data engineers to translate requirements into integrations and automation across contract, procurement, compute data, and finance platforms, with monitoring and governed change controls. - Align Infrastructure, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Legal, and Engineering on decisions and dependencies. Manage scope, risks, vendor dependencies, and change requests; escalate with clear options and business impact. - Lead end-to-end testing, UAT, rollout, training, and handoff to operational owners. Define success measures for traceability, data quality, manual effort, exception resolution, close readiness, and adoption. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 8+ years of experience in project or program management, finance transformation, infrastructure operations, or enterprise systems delivery in complex, scaled environments. - Understanding of compute or infrastructure economics and related finance processes, including commitments, usage-based billing, procurement, accruals, cost allocation, and forecasting. - Experience partnering with software and data engineers to define requirements, resolve tradeoffs, test solutions, and deliver changes into production without direct authority. - A strong process mindset and the ability to connect contractual terms, operational events, financial data, and control requirements into a practical future-state design. - Fluency in data dependencies, system integrations, reconciliation, and data quality. Comfort working with analytical teams and tools such as SQL, Databricks, and BI platforms. - Experience improving workflows through automation or AI, with appropriate human review, controls, exception handling, and operational ownership. - Clear, concise written and verbal communication, including executive updates that explain decisions, risks, business impact, and specific actions needed. - Experience driving complex initiatives through ambiguity and organizational change, with clear evidence of hands-on delivery and adoption. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform. We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work. THE OPPORTUNITY - Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference. - Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks. - Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete. - Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises. - Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance. - Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams. - Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions. - Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production. WHAT YOU BRING - 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time. - Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns. - Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. items.description: About the Team We are building AI systems that help people tackle complex, consequential work in the legal industry. Law demands careful reasoning, precise language, and sound judgment: understanding the facts, identifying the right questions, weighing competing interpretations, and helping clients decide what to do next. We see an opportunity for AI to help legal professionals work with greater rigor and focus more of their time on the problems that matter most. Our team works across Research, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to build AI capabilities and products for legal work. Our customers include the top law firms in the world as well as in-house legal departments of some of the largest businesses in the world. We translate the realities of practice into evaluations, training signals, and useful tools, with the ambition of making AI a trusted part of how lawyers research, analyze, draft, and advise. About the Role We are looking for a Subject Matter Expert in Law who brings the judgment and practical experience developed in a law firm to shaping the next generation of AI. You will help define what excellent legal work looks like, test where our models meet that standard, and turn your findings into better model behavior and product experiences. This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of legal practice and AI development. You will work directly with legal materials, model outputs, evaluation rubrics, and product prototypes. Your expertise will help us tackle some of the hardest questions in legal AI, including how to assess reasoning when there is no single correct answer. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In This Role, You Will: - Define the quality bar for what top-notch legal work looks like, drawing on real matters and the standards lawyers apply to research, analysis, drafting, document review, and client advice. - Design challenging, realistic AI model evaluations with representative facts, source materials, constraints, and deliverables, including cases that test ambiguity, competing arguments, and professional judgment. - Create and review reference work such as research memoranda, contract analyses, redlines, diligence findings, and draft legal documents that demonstrate strong reasoning and practical usefulness. - Develop rubrics that assess legal accuracy, issue spotting, factual grounding, citation validity, jurisdictional context, and the appropriate treatment of uncertainty. - Evaluate model outputs and complete legal workflows, identify recurring failures, and give researchers and engineers specific, actionable feedback supported by examples and corrected work. - Partner with Research on datasets, grading methods, and training tasks or environments that strengthen legal reasoning. Test whether model changes address the underlying problems and improve performance on new cases. - Work with Product and Engineering to identify valuable use cases, prototype workflows, and translate lessons from evaluations into experiences that fit how lawyers actually work. - Collaborate with legal professionals and design partners to refine our standards and test usefulness in practice, applying sound judgment around confidentiality, privilege, data permissions, and professional responsibility. You Might Thrive in This Role If You: - Have practiced law at a law firm, with substantial experience producing and reviewing work for real client matters. We care more about demonstrated judgment and quality of work matter over title or firm pedigree. - Bring deep expertise in one or more practice areas, such as commercial transactions, corporate law, litigation, or regulatory work, and curiosity about workflows beyond your specialty. - Are an excellent legal researcher and writer who can assess authorities, distinguish strong arguments from plausible ones, and explain how facts and context affect a conclusion. - Can make expert judgment explicit: explain why an answer is incomplete, a clause creates risk, or an analysis misses the central issue, and describe what better work would look like. - Enjoy working directly with AI tools, exploring their limits, and testing ideas systematically. You can collaborate closely with technical teams and communicate clearly across disciplines. - Take ownership in ambiguous settings and are willing to build the first version of an evaluation, reference document, rubric, or workflow, then improve it through feedback. - Care deeply about the quality and consequences of legal work, and are motivated by the opportunity to help shape how AI supports the profession. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. About the Role: Glean is looking for a talented Designated Technical Support Engineer to join our rapidly expanding, venture-backed startup. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers. Global advisory and professional services partners help enterprises move from AI strategy to production deployment. This role will lead OpenAI’s global partnership with KPMG, bringing together its advisory, industry, technology transformation, and delivery capabilities with OpenAI’s products and platform.
