It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters. You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together. The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents. Recent recognition: Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 . 2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. We're looking for someone who knows their market, has strong opinions backed by data, and isn't afraid to rethink the approach when a search isn't working. This is a hands-on role with plenty of ownership. You'll source, advise, problem-solve and close, while helping us continuously improve how we hire. Able to demonstrate how AI has improved your work and speak credibly about the crypto ecosystem and where it's heading. items.title: Principal Engineer, Privacy
items.location_text: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is working on frontier AI systems that handle sensitive information at enormous scale. How we protect that data, and how we build privacy into our systems rather than bolting it on afterward, is central to our mission of building AI that is safe and beneficial. As one of our principal privacy engineers, you will be among Anthropic's most senior individual contributors on privacy. You will set technical strategy for how personal data is handled across products, research, and infrastructure, and execute the hardest parts of delivering it. You'll work at the intersection of privacy engineering, distributed systems, and AI safety, on problems without established answers. You will lead through influence, quality of thinking, and trust rather than formal authority. Key responsibilities Define and drive technical strategy and architecture for major areas of privacy, spanning product surfaces, research and training data, internal tooling, and multiple clouds Identify and lead the highest-complexity, company-critical privacy initiatives, guiding engineers across many teams. Be comfortable building the most difficult pieces yourself Architect the primitives that make privacy the default and the safe path the fastest one: data discovery, classification, lineage, purpose-based access control, audit, retention, deletion, and export Turn regulatory, contractual, and consent obligations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, the EU AI Act) into enforced, continuously verified technical controls in partnership with Legal, Policy, and Compliance team Anticipate where AI capabilities, regulation, and customer expectations are heading, and position our systems ahead of them Mentor and develop staff and senior staff engineers, raise the bar for privacy design across engineering, and help hire senior privacy talent Represent Anthropic's privacy engineering to customers, regulators, standards bodies, and the research community Minimum qualifications A track record of operating as a Principal engineer or equivalent: setting technical direction that multiple teams adopted, and delivering company-critical, multi-year initiatives Deep experience applying privacy engineering principles in production systems with a large user base, including privacy by design, data minimization, and purpose limitation Experience architecting data governance infrastructure (classification, lineage, access control, retention, or deletion) across distributed systems and cloud infrastructure at scale Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages; you are effective writing design docs, making architectural calls, and coding in critical paths Understanding of privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA, and the ability to work as a peer with legal and policy experts to turn requirements into technical designs Written and verbal communication that builds alignment across engineering, research, legal, and product teams, up to senior leadership Preferred qualifications Experience building privacy infrastructure or controls for machine learning or AI systems, including training data governance or AI agents Hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (e.g., differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, secure enclaves, secure multi-party computation) Experience establishing or re-architecting a privacy engineering practice under enterprise-customer or regulatory scrutiny Experience briefing executives, auditors, regulators, or enterprise customers on privacy risk, and defending your recommendations under challenge A history of growing engineers into Staff-level and more senior roles Contributions to open-source privacy tooling, privacy research, or industry standards The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $485,000 — $625,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. items.title: Member of Technical Staff (TPM, Compute)
items.description: Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to own how we plan, bring online and run the GPU compute behind every product. Perplexity serves Ask, Computer and API traffic on GPU capacity across multiple cloud and neocloud providers, and demand shifts with every new customer, product launch and model release. Working across engineering, research, Finance and providers, you’ll forecast how much compute we need and when, bring new capacity into production, and own how the fleet performs today, driving fixes when reliability, utilization or cost fall short. The ideal candidate knows GPU fleets, handles technical and commercial details, and is energized by building a function with little precedent. OUR MISSION Perplexity’s mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending. Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they’ve learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality. Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Partner with Finance on the compute demand forecast, 3–12 months out, driven by customer growth, model releases, and post-training and evaluation plans rather than trend lines - Turn the forecast into decisions with Finance and engineering leadership on commitments and budget, checking that new capacity fits the plan before we commit - Bring new capacity online and lead transitions, from contract to production, including provider onboarding, acceptance criteria, migration and decommissioning - Build a single, trusted view of the fleet: capacity, cost, allocation, and uptime, reliability and utilization by provider and workload - Drive daily utilization, reliability and cost-efficiency as core metrics, reclaiming idle capacity and surfacing trade-offs rather than letting them become side effects - Own inference and compute requests end to end: triage and resolve GPU, deployment and quota requests from teams across Perplexity, and build self-serve paths so routine requests no longer need a person in the loop - Manage compute provider relationships, with scorecards and regular reviews of reliability, support and delivery, and use that data to shape how we work with providers over time - Partner with engineering, research, and finance teams on capacity decisions that match the different needs of training, batch inference and real-time production inference - Build the operating system for compute: the processes and tooling to request, plan, allocate and track compute, with clear owners QUALIFICATIONS - 6+ years of technical program management, capacity planning or infrastructure operations in cloud environments, leading programs across teams and vendors - Direct experience with GPU or accelerator fleets across training and inference workloads - Experience working directly with cloud or neocloud providers on reserved capacity, capacity commitments, onboarding or vendor performance management - Experience with infrastructure cost modeling, unit economics or cost attribution in partnership with Finance - Technical depth in cluster management, scheduling and orchestration, and the data skills to build forecasts and dashboards yourself - The judgment to surface hard trade-offs and communicate them clearly from engineers to executives - Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on

Drive advanced workforce data insights . Track and analyze process performance, adoption rates, error trends, and efficiency metrics, translating complex data into strategic recommendations for continuous optimization. Key collaborations This role partners with leaders across HR to ensure that any employee-facing People processes are structured to be scalable, simple to understand, and easy for employees and managers to self-serve. items.title: Senior HR Business Partner
items.description: About the Team The HR Business Partner team at OpenAI supports managers and employees as teams grow, perform and adapt. We work alongside managers at all levels to resolve day-to-day people challenges, build management capability and create the conditions for teams to do their best work. Our expertise spans team effectiveness, talent development, manager coaching, employee relations and change management, grounded in our Contributions & Impact (C&I) culture. We operate with urgency, empathy and sound judgment, valuing sincerity, collaboration and meaningful impact. About the Role We’re looking for a Senior HR Business Partner to support managers and teams across EMEA, with a primary focus on Go-to-Market and responsibility for selected other functions in the region. You’ll provide hands-on support to managers at all levels, owning day-to-day people work and helping teams grow and scale effectively. Your GTM partnership will span teams such as Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships and Marketing. Across your portfolio, you’ll build a deep understanding of business priorities and use that context to prioritise and deliver practical people support. As a hands-on partner to managers at all levels, you will use independent judgment to coach managers, resolve people issues and follow through on day-to-day work as teams scale. You will own delivery across your portfolio, working closely with the International HRBP Leader, Recruiting, Finance, Employment Legal and People centres of expertise, and involving specialist partners when needed. This is an individual contributor role reporting to the International HRBP Leader. Your Key Responsibilities - Own day-to-day HRBP support with a primary focus on GTM. Be a practical point of contact for managers on performance, employee relations, team changes and development. Prioritise issues, agree clear next steps and see them through to resolution as teams scale. - Support teams as they grow. Help managers put agreed team structures and workforce plans into practice, clarify roles and address capacity needs as teams enter new markets and scale existing operations. Coordinate with Finance and Recruiting to support hiring and team changes. - Build manager effectiveness. Coach managers at all levels, from first-time managers to experienced people managers, on feedback, difficult conversations, team dynamics and accountability. Help them address everyday people challenges with clarity and care. - Build capability and succession. Help managers identify skills and development needs across GTM teams. Partner on talent reviews, succession planning, internal mobility and development, with particular attention to roles essential to customer and business outcomes. - Drive performance and rewards decisions. Help managers set clear expectations, address underperformance and recognise contributions consistently. Partner with Compensation and Sales Compensation specialists on people implications of incentive structures, role changes and rewards decisions. - Lead through regional complexity. Guide organisational changes and sensitive employee matters across EMEA, partnering with Employment Legal and Employee Relations specialists. Balance business urgency, local requirements and fair, consistent treatment. - Use insight to act early. Combine workforce data, business context and employee feedback to identify emerging risks, test assumptions and recommend action. Track whether interventions improve capability, retention and team effectiveness. - Scale effective People practices. Partner with global HRBPs and centres of expertise to evolve performance, engagement and talent programmes for EMEA, ensuring regional needs inform global decisions and local delivery remains practical. What You Bring - Substantial HRBP experience. Typically 7–10+ years in HR, including at least five years supporting managers and teams in high-growth, international or complex organisations. We value the scope and impact of your experience. - Commercial understanding. Experience supporting Sales and other go-to-market functions, with an understanding of enterprise sales cycles, customer-facing roles and the people implications of commercial operating models. - Hands-on manager partnership. A record of supporting managers at all levels, resolving day-to-day people issues and owning delivery across a busy portfolio. You can exercise independent judgment, challenge constructively and build trusted relationships. - EMEA experience. Experience across multiple EMEA markets, navigating cultural differences and varied employment environments, with sound judgment about when to involve specialist partners. - Organisational and talent judgment. Practical experience supporting team growth, workforce planning, manager coaching, performance management and talent development, including delivering change through ambiguity. - Analytical and execution strength. The ability to diagnose problems using data and context, make clear recommendations and follow through. You prioritise effectively, take ownership of complex people issues and stay close to the details through resolution. - Integrity and care. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market. Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns. Team Our Raisin UK Finance team is expanding, and we are looking for a hands-on, commercially astute Senior Finance Manager to join our Manchester office. Working directly alongside the Head of Finance UK, this is a high-impact individual contributor role designed for an autonomous operator who thrives on ownership, commercial variety, and cross-functional leadership. With a primary emphasis on FP&A and commercial growth, you will bridge strategic forecasting, business partnering, financial reporting, and process automation in a fast-growing fintech scale-up. Your Responsibilities Financial Reporting, Controlling & Audit Support Own the preparation of timely, high-accuracy monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with UK GAAP/ IFRS, alongside insightful internal management reporting packages. Lead core operational accounting workflows, including revenue invoicing, reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity. Evaluate, establish, and continuously enhance internal financial controls, governance workflows, and accounting procedures. Serve as a key operational point of contact for internal and external auditors, ensuring smooth, efficient audit cycles and statutory compliance. Conduct ad-hoc financial evaluations and commercial business cases requested by local executive leadership and central Group Finance. Partner closely with Business Development (BD) and Relationship Managers (RMs) to model, anticipate, and stress-test future Assets on Platform (AoP) volumes, evaluate growth bottlenecks, and unlock new revenue expansion opportunities. Possess end-to-end knowledge of core accounting functions to provide seamless interim coverage and operational backfill across the finance team when needed. Financial Planning, Forecasting & Commercial Analysis Drive regular financial forecasting cycles, variance analyses, and the annual budgeting process for the UK business. Deliver regular, actionable analyses of trading performance, unit economics, and underlying revenue trends to inform operational strategy. Conduct ad-hoc financial and commercial analyses requested by local leadership and central Group Finance stakeholders. Finance Business Partnering & System Architecture Act as a trusted finance partner to commercial teams and operational leaders, guiding budget holders on spend optimization, ROI, and resource allocation. Champion financial process automation and AI adoption—leveraging modern workflow tools and AI-driven solutions to automate reporting, revenue recognition, invoicing, and billing cycles. Support the ongoing evolution of our controlling systems landscape and internal reporting architecture. Champion financial process automation—particularly around revenue recognition, invoicing, and billing workflows. Support local rollout and implementation of group-wide finance tools and enterprise systems. Your Profile Relevant Experience: 4+ years of progressive experience in roles such as Financial Controller, Senior Management Accountant, or FP&A / Controlling, ideally within a scaling fintech, tech platform, or dynamic high-growth business. Equally ideal opportunity for anyone currently operating at a Managerial grade within a Big 4 accounting/audit firm and considering a change. A recognized professional accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA) is a distinct advantage. Technical Accounting Standards: Deep practical understanding of UK GAAP; working knowledge of IFRS is highly desirable. Analytical & Modeling Proficiency: Strong quantitative mindset with advanced financial modeling capabilities, high attention to detail, and a structured, self-directed working style. Systems & Digital Affinity: Strong tech acumen and proficiency with spreadsheet tools (MS Excel, Google Sheets) and modern ERP software (experience with Oracle NetSuite is a strong plus). Cross-Functional Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to distill complex financial contexts into clear, actionable narratives for non-finance stakeholders. Agility & Ownership: Proven ability to operate effectively and maintain exceptional accuracy in a fast-paced environment where problem-solving, adaptability, and execution matter. Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us!
